problem.text: Quantization lacked the image-dump hooks added here for inspecting original and regularized weight matrices.

reasoning.text: The implementation makes visualization opt-in and copies tensors before modifying their display values, separating diagnostic normalization from quantization data.

impact.text: Image dumping introduces CPU copies, color-array construction and synchronous image writes. These support the documentation's qualitative memory, disk-space and latency warnings; their magnitude is not measured.

source_notes.text: Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” reports a native-extension import failure and the reporter's environment workaround. Its connection here is only inferred from the matching convert.py import line, not evidence that image dumping addresses that failure.

limitations: No repository conversion, GPU operation, matplotlib colormap or Pillow image save was executed. Installed-library compatibility and filesystem behavior remain unverified.
The scalar check uses Python floating-point arithmetic and supplied statistics, not PyTorch float32 reductions or image encoding.

claims.text: The parser accepts -img and --image_dump. prepare copies the current invocation's flag into image_dump for both new and resumed jobs; prepare_env creates work_dir/images even when dumping is disabled.

main dumps loaded Linear quantization targets selected by a truthy qmap and non-null device, before swapping their original weights to CPU. Original images use images/<linear.key>.jpg. A second path, images/<linear.key>.reg.jpg, passes through Linear.convert_exl3 to quantize_exl3, where weight_r is saved after regularize and before ldlq. These are pre-quantization diagnostics, not pictures of reconstructed quantized weights.

Both conversion APIs append optional save_reg=None parameters. save_tensor_image imports matplotlib.cm and PIL.Image only when called, detaches and copies its input to CPU float32, clamps to mean ± 3 standard deviations, and normalizes by the resulting six-standard-deviation span plus 1e-8. It applies gnuplot2, drops alpha, multiplies RGB by 255, converts to uint8 and saves the image.

A scalar transcription with mean 0 and standard deviation 1 mapped values at or below -3 to 0, the mean to approximately 0.5, and values at or above 3 to approximately 1. A finite constant input with zero standard deviation mapped to 0 because of the denominator epsilon.

Independent normalization emphasizes each matrix's internal pattern rather than preserving a shared absolute color scale between original and regularized weights. Clipping also deliberately discards outlier magnitude in the visualization.

findings.description: The added documentation overstates coverage as “all tensors” and omits the leading -- from the long option.
findings.trigger: Following the new image-dump option description.
findings.expected_behavior: Documentation names --image_dump and describes images of selected linear weights and their regularized forms.
findings.actual_behavior: The text says “-img / image_dump” and “all tensors,” whereas the parser registers --image_dump and main only dumps its selected Linear quantization targets.

verification.description: Compared the added documentation with the parser registration and the linear-target selection surrounding the image writes.
verification.limits: No CLI invocation or image generation was executed.

annotation.summary: Adds optional JPEG diagnostics for original and regularized linear weights, using per-tensor clipped color normalization.
